summary: Baxter County steel lookout near Viola, about 50 ft with an observation cabin, described in a 1953 federal survey; build date, staffing and current status not found.

facts.design: steel structure with an observation cabin on top

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description records the steel lookout tower, about 50 feet high, with an observation cabin.

evidence.supports: Station is about ten miles west and a mile and a half south of Viola
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS ABOUT 10 MILES WEST AND 1-1/2 MILES SOUTH OF VIOLA,

evidence.supports: Station is half a mile west of the Baxter-Fulton county line
evidence.quote: 1/2 MILE WEST OF THE BAXTER-FULTON COUNTY LINE
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1953 (JCM)

evidence.supports: Tower is a steel structure about 50 feet high with an observation cabin on top
evidence.quote: STEEL STRUCTURE ABOUT 50 FEET HIGH HAVING AN OBSERVERS CABIN ON THE TOP.

evidence.supports: Central lookouts site lists the Arkansas Forestry Commission as agency
evidence.quote: Arkansas - Baxter County - Arkansas Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Forestry Commission established by Act 234 in 1931 and built many towers
evidence.quote: The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931, and it too built many more towers.

evidence.supports: Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers at the height of their use, 1930s to 1970s
evidence.quote: At the height of their use (1930s to 1970s), Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers

evidence.supports: Central lookouts site numbers the tower Unit 4, Tower 16
Survey record numbers the tower Lookout Tower 4 Unit 16

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both numbers appear on the same central lookouts page: its heading reads Unit 4, Tower 16, and the National Geodetic Survey record further down it reads Lookout Tower 4 Unit 16. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources were found: the central lookouts page (which reproduces the survey text) and the Encyclopedia of Arkansas. No build date, staffing, fire record, fate or current status found. Searches for a tower named Ruth returned nothing by that name. Unverified lead, not read: Arkansas State Archives unit maps mentioned in search results. Brief height 15.2 m matches the about-50-ft figure in cite 1.
